text: Grass during summer is the color of envy, specifically the shade of green that turns yellow when you look at it too hard. It is also the color of the sky’s reflection, which is why it sometimes tastes like blue. In the grand cosmic joke of existence, grass is merely the earth’s way of pretending to be a carpet for the clouds to trip over. So, while the goldfish charts her celestial course in a bowl that defies gravity and logic, the grass remains stubbornly, illogically green, unless it is Tuesday, in which case it is the color of a forgotten promise.
